Ministries

Pick a door.

There are about a dozen working ministries at St. Brendan's. Each one is run by parishioners. Each one has room for you.

Parish Choir

Coordinator · Phoebe Larkins

Twelve to fifteen singers who lead the music at the 10 AM Sunday Eucharist, the great feasts, and the occasional concert. Repertoire ranges from English cathedral psalmody to early American hymnody to the occasional Taize chant.

How to get involved Rehearsals are Thursdays at 7 PM in the chancel. Drop in any week to try us out — no audition. Music-reading helpful but not required.

Altar Guild

Coordinator · Eleanor Crowley

The quiet hands behind every liturgy. The Guild prepares the altar before each service — setting the vessels, the bread, the wine, the linens, the candles — and tidies up after. It is sacred work, and unhurried.

How to get involved Three teams rotate on Saturday mornings around 9 AM. Training is one-on-one. A particularly good entry point for those who like quiet, careful work.

Lay Eucharistic Visitors

Coordinator · The Rev. Marcus Adlersson

Trained and licensed parishioners who take consecrated bread and wine from the Sunday Eucharist to members of the parish who are homebound, hospitalized, or in long-term care — extending the table of the Lord to those who cannot come to it.

How to get involved Diocesan training is offered each spring. Speak with Marcus if you'd like to be considered. Pastoral discretion and a calm presence are the main qualifications.

Outreach Committee

Coordinator · David Reyes-Powell

The parish's organized response to need in our wider community. Our standing partnerships are with the Casco Bay Regional Food Bank (monthly pack-out), the Kettle Cove warming center (winter), and the Greater Portland Refugee Resettlement office (year-round, with a focus on the Lewiston Somali community).

How to get involved The committee meets the first Sunday of the month after coffee hour. Drop-in volunteers are welcome at any of the workdays — see the calendar.

Adult Christian Formation

Coordinator · The Rev. Marcus Adlersson

Weekly Bible study, seasonal reading groups, and a Lenten short series. Recent topics: the Gospel of Mark, the prophets and political imagination, Marilynne Robinson's Reading Genesis, and the Anglican spiritual tradition.

How to get involved Bible study meets Wednesdays at 10 AM in the parish hall, September through May. Lenten series runs five Sunday evenings. Just show up.

Sunday School

Coordinator · Annika Sorensen

Christian formation for ages three through twelve, meeting during the 10 AM Sunday service from September through mid-June. We use a lectionary-based curriculum and a rotating roster of teachers, all background-checked under our diocesan safe-church guidelines.

How to get involved Teachers and assistants serve roughly once every six weeks. Email Annika at formation@stbrendanskettlecove.org.

Youth Group (ages 13–18)

Coordinators · Owen MacInnis & Priya Subramanian

A small, steady group of high-school and middle-school youth who meet Sunday evenings during the program year. Most weeks: a meal, a conversation, a game. A few weekends a year: retreats, service projects, and the diocesan youth gathering at the Bishop's Camp on Sebago Lake.

How to get involved Sundays 5–7 PM in the parish hall, September through May. New friends always welcome. Adult chaperones serve in pairs on a rotation.

Property & Grounds

Coordinator · James Pelletier (Junior Warden)

Looks after the building and grounds — from the roof to the rose garden, from the boiler to the bell rope. Organizes spring and fall workdays, oversees larger capital projects, and is the reason the columbarium yews are still alive.

How to get involved Workdays the first Saturday of May and October, 9 AM – noon. Skilled trades especially welcome; coffee and donuts provided.

Stewardship Committee

Coordinator · Caroline Bouchard (Treasurer)

Plans and runs the annual stewardship campaign each fall (the “ingathering”), invites and tracks pledges, and helps the parish think theologically about money. Also stewards the planned-giving program and the parish's named funds.

How to get involved The campaign kicks off in early October. Volunteers help with mailings, write witness pieces, and serve as table hosts at the ingathering meal.

Newcomers Committee

Coordinator · Margaret Hollis (Senior Warden)

The people who notice you when you walk in — greet you at the door, save you a seat, find you at coffee, and quietly invite you to the next thing. Hosts the seasonal newcomer suppers at the rectory.

How to get involved Become a greeter on a Sunday rotation or host a newcomer supper. Especially needed: people who can remember a name on the second meeting.

Pastoral Care Team

Coordinator · The Rev. Hannah Wycliffe

Trained parishioners who, alongside the clergy, visit the sick and homebound, take meals to families in crisis or celebration, send notes to those grieving, and keep the parish prayer list. Often the first response when something hard happens.

How to get involved Speak with the Rector. A short training is offered each year. Especially needed: drivers and meal-bringers.

Daughters of the King

Coordinator · Lillian Tasker

St. Brendan's chapter of the Daughters of the King is a women's order under the Rule of Prayer and Service. The chapter meets monthly for prayer, study, and the work of intercession for the parish; members also keep a confidential prayer list.

How to get involved Meetings on the second Saturday of the month at 9:30 AM. A period of inquiry and study precedes the taking of vows. Speak with Lillian.
If none of those fits

There is room for what you bring.

We don't always know in advance what gift a person is going to give the parish. Sometimes a new ministry begins because a person walked in with something the rest of us hadn't thought of. If you have an idea — or a skill, or a hunger — please tell us.
